descripcion: Construction constants for the base: regolith, excavation, pads, roads, ice, water plant, crops. Each value carries a literal quotation checked against its source by scripts/verificar_citas.py.

constantes.texto: bulk density of lunar regolith at the surface (Lunar Sourcebook, p. 494)
constantes.organismo: NASA Johnson Space Center (Connolly, IEEE Aerospace Conference)
constantes.cita: approximately 1.30 g/cm at the surface, increases rapidly to 1.52 g/cm at a depth of 10 cm, then more gradually to 1.83 g/cm at a depth of 100 cm.
constantes.nota: the superscript 3 of g/cm3 is lost in the PDF text; the sentence states g/cm3

constantes.organismo: NASA Johnson Space Center (Connolly, IEEE Aerospace Conference)

constantes.unidad: g/cm3; z, a, b in cm
constantes.texto: rho(z) = rho_inf (z + a) / (z + b), z = depth below the surface in cm
constantes.organismo: NASA Johnson Space Center (Connolly, IEEE Aerospace Conference)
constantes.cita: Density versus depth can be expressed by the following hyperbolic relationship: r = 1.92 ( z + 12.2 ) / ( z + 18 ) where z = depth in lunar surface (cm)
constantes.nota: the Greek rho extracts as 'r' in the PDF text

constantes.texto: IPEx design goal: regolith excavated in a single lunar day
constantes.organismo: NASA (IPEx project page)
constantes.cita: The system is designed to excavate up to 10,000 kg of regolith, similar to the weight of 20 adult elephants, in a single lunar day.
constantes.nota: page undated. The 2024 IPEx design paper (ipex in equipo.json) gives 10,000 kg over an 11-day reference mission at 42 kg/h

constantes.texto: water ice in the regolith at the LCROSS impact site
constantes.organismo: NASA LCROSS team (Colaprete et al., Science 330, 463)
constantes.cita: the concentration of water ice in the regolith at the LCROSS impact site is estimated to be 5.6

lugar.nombre: LCROSS impact site, permanently shadowed floor of Cabeus crater (not Shackleton)
lugar.cita: first revealed Cabeus crater (84.9 deg S, 35.5degW) as having the highest inferred hydrogen on the Moon

lugar_ref.cita: a spent Centaur rocket struck the persistently shadowed region within the lunar south pole crater Cabeus

constantes.nota: the paper gives ± 2.9 % as uncertainty; the ± glyph extracts as 'T', so the uncertainty is left out (not citable by the checker)

constantes.texto: LCROSS total water, ice plus vapour (range)
constantes.organismo: NASA Ames Research Center (EGU General Assembly abstract)
constantes.cita: the LCROSS impact yielded total water estimates, ice plus vapor, of between 3 and 10 wt%.

constantes.texto: surfaces much warmer than ~100 K (maximum temperature) do not keep surface water ice
constantes.organismo: Fisher et al., Icarus (LOLA and Diviner; NASA GSFC co-authors, NTRS copy)
constantes.cita: prevents surfaces that experience temperatures much above 100K from preserving surface water ice due to rapid sublimation loss

ref.cita: surfaces that never exceed temperatures ~100K are able to preserve surface frost over geologically significant time periods against sublimation

constantes.texto: baseline: 15 t of water collected and processed in 225 days (for 10 t of oxygen)
constantes.organismo: NASA Glenn Research Center and Johnson Space Center (Kleinhenz & Paz, ASCEND)
constantes.cita: must be produced in 225 days. Therefore 15 mT of water would need to be collected and processed.

constantes.texto: total required power, baseline (surface power system not included)
constantes.organismo: NASA Glenn Research Center and Johnson Space Center (Kleinhenz & Paz, ASCEND)
constantes.cita: The baseline solution resulted in a system mass of 5 mT and a total required power of 68 kW.

constantes.texto: system mass, baseline (5 mT)
constantes.organismo: NASA Glenn Research Center and Johnson Space Center (Kleinhenz & Paz, ASCEND)
constantes.cita: The baseline solution resulted in a system mass of 5 mT and a total required power of 68 kW.

constantes.texto: approximately 20 kW each: hydrogen liquefaction, electrolysis, water extractor
constantes.organismo: NASA Glenn Research Center and Johnson Space Center (Kleinhenz & Paz, ASCEND)
constantes.cita: The majority of the required power was with three subsystems at approximately 20 kW each: hydrogen liquefaction, electrolysis, and the water extractor subsystem.

constantes.texto: water extraction efficiency (75 %)
constantes.organismo: NASA Glenn Research Center and Johnson Space Center (Kleinhenz & Paz, ASCEND)
constantes.cita: Losses in the water extraction and capture process (e.g. sublimation during excavation, line losses, etc) are captured in the extraction efficiency parameter, which is set at 75%.

constantes.texto: LADI auger dryer goal: water extraction rate (cancelled at TRL 4)
